column3: NASB follows the critical text (“For”); “ignorant” is rendered “unaware.”
NASB follows the critical text.
Close to the Greek.
NASB renders “accompanying” as “which followed them.”
NASB renders “strewn” as “laid low.”
NASB renders “types” as “examples” and “desirers of evil things” as “crave evil things”; it adds “happened.”
NASB follows the critical text (“as”); it adds “were,” and the quotation is in capitals. Stray spacing around the quotation marks appears in the NASB text.
NASB follows the critical text without “in”; “commit sexual immorality” is rendered “act immorally.”
NASB reads “the Lord,” following other manuscripts; the critical text has “Christ.” “Test” is rendered “try.”
NASB follows the critical text; “the Destroyer” is lowercase.
NASB follows the critical text; “typologically” is rendered “as an example,” and “admonition” is “instruction.”
NASB renders “thinking to have stood” as “thinks he stands.”
NASB renders “seized” as “overtaken” and “the escape” as “the way of escape.”
Close to the Greek.
NASB renders “sensible ones” as “wise men.”
NASB renders “participation” as “sharing.”
NASB renders “loaf” as “bread.”
NASB follows the critical text; “Israel according to flesh” is rendered “the nation Israel,” and “fellow partakers” is “sharers.”
Close to the Greek.
NASB follows the critical text; it renders “Rather” as “No, but I say.”
Close to the Greek.
NASB casts the second question as “are we?”
NASB follows the critical text without “to me.”
NASB follows the critical text without “each”; it adds “good” and renders “the other” as “his neighbor.”
NASB renders “inquiring” as “asking questions” and “on account of conscience” as “for conscience' sake.”
The quotation is in capitals except “Lord's”; “the fullness of it” is rendered “ALL IT CONTAINS.”
NASB follows the critical text without “now.”
NASB reads “meat sacrificed to idols,” the word of other manuscripts; the critical text has “offered in sacrifice.” It follows the critical text without repeating “the earth is the Lord's.”
NASB renders “I am saying” as “I mean” and adds “man's.”
NASB follows the critical text; “denigrated” is rendered “slandered.”
